title: M/S Maya Foods v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pritinker Diwaker, C.J.; Ashutosh Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner permitted to apply under Section 6.5 within 15 days, with orders expected in one month.
headnote: Writ petition disposed of because the petitioners have an alternative remedy of an application under Section 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner may approach Respondent No. 2 within 15 days, and Respondent No. 2 is expected to pass appropriate orders within one month of service of a certified copy. Merits were not examined.
facts: M/S Maya Foods and another petitioned the Allahabad High Court against Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and another. The order does not recite the underlying electricity grievance. Counsel for the petitioners said the petitioner had been running from pillar to post for many years and that the authorities were still not deciding the case. Counsel for the electricity department stated that if the petitioner approached Respondent No. 2, appropriate orders would be passed on the application.

holding_units.topic: Alternative remedy by application under Supply Code Section 6.5
holding_units.holding: On the facts narrated in the writ petition, the petitioners have an alternative remedy of filing an application under Section 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of by permitting the petitioner to approach Respondent No. 2 within 15 days; Respondent No. 2 is expected to pass appropriate orders on that application within one month of service of a certified copy of the order.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench declined to decide the grievance in writ and disposed of the petition by sending the petitioner to Respondent No. 2 under Section 6.5, with a 15-day approach window and an expectation of orders within one month.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioners' electricity grievance against the licensee
not_decided.note: Left to Respondent No. 2 to pass appropriate orders on an application under Section 6.5; the Court neither granted nor refused the underlying relief.
